item.text: {"case_id":"SPR00201","decision":"candidate","candidate_ranking":["C20","C13","C08"],"selected_candidate_label":"C20","confidence":0.88,"relationship_type":"both","rationale":"C20 is the strongest plausible drafting template. Both directives implement the same Alaska admission statute through a recital-driven presidential proclamation: they identify statutory conditions, recite facts showing those conditions have been satisfied, and then formally declare the resulting legal transition. The child adapts C20's machinery from admission of Alaska to activation of Alaska's new federal district court and termination of the territorial court. C13 shares the statute, Alaska-transition setting, and determination of terminated and successor functions, but its sectioned delegation-and-property-transfer scheme is less similar. C08 has a comparable statutory-recital-to-termination proclamation structure but concerns unrelated military jurisdiction and uses less closely parallel machinery.","shared_material":[{"child_excerpt":"WHEREAS the act of July 7, 1958, 72 Stat. 339, relating to the admission of the State of Alaska into the Union, provides that ... unless the President, by Executive order, shall sooner proclaim that the United States District Court for the District of Alaska ... is prepared to assume the functions imposed upon it","parent_excerpt":"Whereas the Congress of the United States by the act approved on July 7, 1958 (72 Stat. 339) ... provided for the admission of the State of Alaska into the Union ... upon compliance with certain procedural requirements specified in that act","explanation":"Both begin from the same Alaska admission act and frame presidential action as recognition that statutory transition conditions have been fulfilled."},{"child_excerpt":"WHEREAS ... I have appointed ... the Honorable Walter N. Hodge ... and he has taken his oath of office; and WHEREAS Judge Hodge has appointed ... other court officers; and WHEREAS the United States District Court for the District of Alaska is now prepared","parent_excerpt":"Whereas it appears from information before me that ... [the required propositions were approved and an election held] ... and Whereas I find and announce that the people of Alaska have duly adopted the propositions ... and have duly elected the officers required","explanation":"Each directive supplies a sequence of factual recitals establishing institutional readiness and fulfillment of the act's prerequisites."},{"child_excerpt":"NOW, THEREFORE ... I hereby proclaim that the United States District Court for the District of Alaska is prepared to assume the functions imposed upon it. Accordingly, the Jurisdiction of the District Court for the Territory of Alaska ... [is] now terminated.","parent_excerpt":"Now, Therefore ... do hereby declare and proclaim that the procedural requirements imposed by the Congress on the State of Alaska ... have been complied with in all respects and that admission ... is now accomplished.","explanation":"The operative clauses use closely parallel declaratory-proclamation language to trigger a legal transition after finding statutory conditions satisfied."}]}
